messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - Opens the first volume of a multi-volume ZIP (“apache-maven-2.2.1.zip.001”) as a stream.
  - Iterates through several valid entries successfully.
  - Moves to the last entry, which is truncated because the rest of the compressed data is in the next volume.
  - Attempts to read the last entry, expecting an IOException with message “Truncated ZIP file.” Instead, read returns 0, causing the loop to exit without an exception, and the test fails.

- Relevant code behavior:
  - ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int):
    - For DEFLATED entries (the typical case here), it feeds input to the Inflater when inf.needsInput() is true by calling fill().
    - It then calls inf.inflate(...).
    - If read == 0 and inf.finished() is true, it returns -1 (end-of-entry).
    - Otherwise, it returns the number of bytes decompressed (which can be 0).
  - ZipArchiveInputStream.fill():
    - Reads more compressed data into an internal buffer: lengthOfLastRead = in.read(buf).
    - If lengthOfLastRead > 0, it sets the inflater input (inf.setInput(...)).
    - If in.read returns -1 (EOF), fill() does nothing—no exception is thrown and no state is recorded indicating truncation.
  - ZipArchiveInputStream.readFully(byte[]):
    - Used for headers and extra fields, throws EOFException on premature EOF.
    - But this is not used for the compressed data of an entry—only for headers, so truncation during data read is not detected here.

- How the bug occurs on truncated data:
  - For the truncated final entry, the inflater still “needs input” but the underlying stream has hit EOF in the middle of the compressed data.
  - fill() calls in.read(buf) and gets -1. Since lengthOfLastRead is not > 0, it does not set new input on the inflater and does not raise an error.
  - Back in read(), inf.inflate(...) returns 0 because there is no input and inflating cannot progress; inf.finished() is false because it hasn’t reached a valid end-of-stream marker.
  - read() returns 0 rather than -1 or throwing an exception. This matches the bug report: “All calls to read() will return 0 bytes read. They will not return -1 nor throw any exception.”
  - The test’s while-loop exits (read == 0), and the code reaches fail("shouldn't be able to read from truncated entry").

- Secondary effect on getNextEntry():
  - If client code attempts to advance to the next entry after a truncated read, getNextZipEntry() first calls closeEntry(), which calls skip(Long.MAX_VALUE).
  - skip uses read() to consume the rest of the entry. With the current behavior, read() returns 0 repeatedly (never -1), so skip can spin forever or block, and closeEntry() won’t complete. The test expects an exception at this point as well; with the current code, it may hang instead of throwing.

- Root cause:
  - There is no detection of premature EOF during entry data decompression for DEFLATED entries. When the underlying input reaches EOF before the data stream is complete:
    - fill() silently does nothing (no input provided to the inflater and no error signaling).
    - read() sees inflate() return 0 and inf.finished() is false; it returns 0, not -1 or an IOException.
  - In contrast, header reads use readFully() and properly throw EOFException on truncation.

- Expected behavior (per test and report):
  - When the entry’s compressed data is truncated, read() should throw an IOException with message “Truncated ZIP file” (rather than returning 0 or -1).
  - Subsequent attempts to getNextEntry() should also fail with an exception rather than hanging.

In summary, the logic in ZipArchiveInputStream for DEFLATED entries does not handle the case where the underlying stream reaches EOF before the inflater finishes. Because fill() suppresses EOF and read() returns 0 when inflate cannot make progress and isn’t finished, truncated archives are not reported, matching both the issue description and the failing test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
